questionText: With reference to Liquid tree, consider the following statements: 1. It improves air quality by producing pure oxygen without using photosynthesis. 2. India is the first country to introduce this concept. 3. It is more efficient than trees in terms of its functioning. How many of the above statements are correct?
mnemonic_hint: Think 'LIQO' as 'LIquid-algae-Oxygen'—it uses algae to scrub air, but remember Serbia, not India, pioneered it.

questionText: Consider the following: 1. Central Pollution Control Board 2. Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee 3. National Coastal Zone Management Authority How many of the above are constituted under the Environment Protection Act of 1986?
concepts: Legal framework for environmental governance in India
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'C-G-N' (Central, Genetic, National) are all EPA-born: CPCB (Water Act), GEAC (EPA), and NCZMA (EPA) - wait, CPCB is Water Act, so only GEAC and NCZMA are EPA!

questionText: Consider the following statements: 1. The Central Ground Water Authority was constituted under the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974. 2. It works under the administrative control of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mnemonic_hint: CGWA is a 'Child' of the Environment Protection Act (EPA 1986) and now lives under the 'Jal Shakti' roof, not the Ministry of Environment.

questionText: With reference to the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, consider the following statements: 1. It was proposed by the European Union at the 27th edition of the UNFCCC Conference of Parties (COP27). 2. It aims to tax extremely carbon-intensive products. 3. India and China have signed and ratified this mechanism. How many of the above statements are correct?
mnemonic_hint: Think of CBAM as 'Carbon Border-Tax Against Manufacturers'—it's an EU-led trade tool, not a global treaty signed by everyone.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding Biodiversity beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ): 1. Unlike United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), it is a legally binding treaty. 2. Areas beyond national jurisdiction (ABNJ), occupies nearly 2/3 of the ocean. 3. It will play a crucial role in achieving the recent ambitious “30x30” initiative. How many of the above statements are correct?
mnemonic_hint: BBNJ: Beyond Borders, New Jurisdiction—protecting the 2/3rds of the ocean to hit the 30x30 target.

questionText: Keeling Curve, sometimes seen in the news recently, is associated with?
options: a) Representation of expansion of the Universe in light years.
b) Measurement of Carbon Dioxide in the atmosphere.
c) A chain of volcanoes formed in the Pacific Ring of Fire.
d) Measurement of methane emissions from horticulture.
mnemonic_hint: Think of Charles Keeling 'Keeping' track of the rising CO2 levels in the air.

questionText: Recently a new species “Manis Mysteria” has been discovered by scientists. They are known for their elusive nature and status as the most trafficked mammals in the world. Which species has been in the above description?
mnemonic_hint: Think of 'Manis' as the genus name for Pangolins, which are 'Man-made' targets for illegal trafficking.

questionText: Consider the following: 1. Wood 2. Wheat 3. Corn 4. Sugar beet 5. Cassava Which of the above can be used to produce ethanol?
mnemonic_hint: Think of 'W-W-C-S-C' (Wood, Wheat, Corn, Sugar beet, Cassava) as the 'Fuel-Five' that can all be fermented into ethanol.

questionText: Consider the following statements: 1. The total forest and tree cover in India is more than 30 percent of the geographical area of the country. 2. Arunachal Pradesh has the largest Recorded Forest Area as well as the largest Forest cover in India. 3. Recorded Forest Areas are notified under the Indian Forests Act of 1927. How many of the above statements are correct?
concepts: Geographical distribution of forests in India
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'MP-RFA': Madhya Pradesh has the largest Recorded Forest Area, while Arunachal Pradesh has the largest forest cover in the North East, but not the whole of India.

questionText: Consider the following statements: 1. The United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) is the only legally binding framework set up to address desertification and the effects of drought. 2. The Bonn Challenge is a global goal to bring 350 million hectares of degraded and deforested landscapes into restoration by 2030. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
sub_topic: International Environmental Conventions and Restoration Initiatives
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'UN-Desert-Binding' for UNCCD and 'Bonn-350' for the 350 million hectare goal.

questionText: With reference to the ‘Global Methane Pledge Energy Pathway’, consider the following statements: 1. It was launched by India in collaboration with the European Union. 2. It encourages all nations to capture the maximum potential of cost-effective methane mitigation in the oil and gas sectors. 3. It works in collaboration with the International Methane Emissions Observatory. How many of the above statements are correct?
mnemonic_hint: Think 'US-EU' for the Pledge (not India), and remember that the 'IMEO' acts as the data-tracking brain for the pathway.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding the Global biodiversity Framework Fund (GBF) Fund: 1. It has been established under the Green Climate Fund. 2. The GBF Fund is uniquely dedicated to support the implementation of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. 3. Canada and China were two initial contributors to start its capitalisation. How many of the above statements are correct?
sub_topic: International Environmental Conventions and Funding Mechanisms
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'GBF-GEF': The Global Biodiversity Framework Fund is managed by the Global Environment Facility, not the Green Climate Fund.

questionText: With reference to the Green Grids Initiative, consider the following statements: 1. It aims to build a framework for global cooperation on the effective utilisation of renewable resources. 2. It was launched by Germany and France at the UNFCCC Conference of Parties 26, 2021. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
concepts: One Sun One World One Grid (OSOWOG)
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'GGI-OSOWOG' was launched by India and the UK (not Germany/France) to connect the world's sun-drenched regions.

questionText: Consider the following: 1. Least Developed Countries Fund 2. Special Climate Change Fund 3. Adaptation Fund 4. Capacity-building Initiative for Transparency (CBIT) 5. Green Climate Fund How many of the above are managed by the Global Environment Facility (GEF)?
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'L-S-C' (Least Developed, Special Climate, Capacity-building) are GEF-managed, while Green Climate Fund and Adaptation Fund are independent entities under the UNFCCC.

questionText: Which of the following techniques can be employed to control Oil Spills? 1. Bioremediation 2. Dispersion 3. Oil Booms 4. Burning Select the correct answer using the code given below:
sub_topic: Marine Pollution and Oil Spill Management
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'B-D-O-B' (Bioremediation, Dispersion, Oil Booms, Burning) as the 'Big Disaster Oil Battle' plan.

questionText: Consider the following: 1. Supply to Municipal corporations 2. Creation of water parks 3. Supply for irrigation purposes 4. Groundwater recharge How many of the above are the applications of coal mine water?
sub_topic: Sustainable Mining and Water Resource Management
mnemonic_hint: Think of 'M-I-G-S': Municipal, Irrigation, Groundwater, and Sports/Parks.

questionText: Which of the following electrical and electronic equipment (EEE) are covered under the E-waste (Management) Rules 2022? 1. Nuclear medicine equipment 2. Radiotherapy equipment 3. Magnetic Resonance Imaging 4. Waste batteries 5. Refrigerators Select the correct answer using the code given below:
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'RE-MED': Refrigerators, Equipment (Medical), and Electronic Devices are the core focus of the 2022 Rules.

questionText: Consider the following statements with reference to the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 in India: 1. The producers and battery importers are responsible for the collection and recycling of battery wastes. 2. They apply to automotive batteries and industrial batteries only. 3. They provide for the disposal of used batteries through incineration. How many of the above statements are correct?
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'ALL-E': Rules cover ALL battery types (EV, portable, industrial) and focus on EPR (Extended Producer Responsibility) rather than incineration.

questionText: “Belem Declaration” seen in news is related to:
sub_topic: International Environmental Agreements and Indigenous Rights
mnemonic_hint: Think of 'Belem' as 'Belonging'—the declaration is about the Indigenous people belonging to and protecting the Amazon.

questionText: Consider the following statements with reference to the Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2022: 1. It has banned the manufacture and sale of plastic carry bags of less than 120 microns. 2. The producers and brand owners are required to provide the details of recycling certificates only from registered recyclers. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mnemonic_hint: Think '120 is the limit for the bag, and the recycler must be on the tag' to remember the micron limit and registration requirement.

questionText: Consider the following statements with reference to Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD) and REDD+: 1. While REDD focuses on preventing deforestation, REDD+ aims at sustainable forest conservation. 2. REDD+ provides financial incentives to developing countries for enhancing the quality of forests for increased carbon storage. 3. The implementation of REDD+ activities is voluntary and depends on the national circumstances. How many of the above statements are correct?
sub_topic: International Climate Agreements and Forest Conservation
mnemonic_hint: Remember REDD+ as 'REDD PLUS': Plus stands for Preservation, Logging reduction, Under-growth management, and Sequestration.

questionText: Consider the following statements with reference to the Paris Agreement of 2015: 1. It is a legally binding international treaty on climate change. 2. It is mandatory for all Parties to the agreement to prepare and maintain a Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC). Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'P-A-N': Paris Agreement requires NDCs, which are mandatory to prepare, but the specific targets within them are not legally binding.

questionText: Consider the following statements with reference to “The Economics of Ecosystems and Biodiversity (TEEB)”: 1. It is an initiative hosted by the United Nations Environment Programme and World Bank. 2. Its objective is to mainstream the values of biodiversity into decision-making at all levels. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mnemonic_hint: Think of TEEB as 'The Economics of Ecosystems and Biodiversity'—it is UNEP-hosted (not World Bank) to make nature's value 'TEEB-le' (visible) in policy.

questionText: Consider the following statements with reference to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC): 1. It was created by the World Meteorological Organisation and the United Nations Environment Programme. 2. All member countries of the United Nations can participate in the IPCC Plenary sessions. 3. It conducts its own research on the impacts of climate change. How many of the above statements are correct?
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'IPCC is a Reviewer, not a Researcher': It synthesizes existing science rather than conducting new experiments.

questionText: Which one of the following statements best describes the term ‘Ecological Footprint’?
options: a) It is a metric that comprehensively compares human demand for nature against nature’s capacity to regenerate.
b) It is an increase in population size at a rate proportional to the size of the population.
c) It is the ratio of the rate of change of ecological assets with the rate of population growth.
d) It is the maximum number of individuals in a single population that a given environment can sustain at a given time.
mnemonic_hint: Think of 'Footprint' as the 'size of the shoe' you leave on Earth; the bigger the footprint, the more nature you consume.

questionText: Consider the following statements with reference to Natural farming and Organic farming: 1. Unlike natural farming, organic farming restricts farmers from using pesticides on plants. 2. Both use organic fertilizers and manures as a nutrient in the soil. 3. Both farming techniques use ploughing and weeding activities How many of the above statements are correct?
mnemonic_hint: Organic allows 'bought' organic inputs, Natural relies on 'nature's own' inputs (no ploughing/weeding).

questionText: With reference to the ‘Global Shield Against Climate Risks Initiative’, consider the following statements: 1. It is an insurance-based finance mechanism for loss and damage that occurs during climate disasters. 2. It is a joint initiative of the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) and the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mnemonic_hint: Think of the 'Global Shield' as a 'G7-V20' partnership—it protects against climate damage, not CDRI-UNFCCC.

questionText: With reference to Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act 2023, consider the following statements: 1. Consent of Gram Sabha is mandatory for the settlement of claims of forest dwellers. 2. Strategic projects related to national security within 10 km of the International Borders are exempted from provisions of the Act. 3. Surveys and investigations in forest areas will not be considered non-forestry activities. How many of the above statements are correct?
mnemonic_hint: Remember '100km' for security, 'Gram Sabha' for rights, and 'Survey' as non-forest: 100-G-S.

questionText: Consider the following: 1. Atmospheric moisture harvesting 2. Highly brackish groundwater 3. Agricultural drainage water 4. Physical transportation of icebergs 5. Snowfall 6. Ballast water Which of the following can be considered as an example of unconventional water resources?
mnemonic_hint: Think of 'AB-HAPS': Atmospheric, Ballast, Highly brackish, Agricultural drainage, Physical iceberg, Snowfall.

questionText: Consider the following statements regarding Global Infrastructure Resilience Report: 1. It has been launched by the World Economic Forum. 2. This report will be released Biennially. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mnemonic_hint: Think of 'GIRR' as 'Global Infrastructure Resilience Report'—it is launched by the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI), not the WEF.

questionText: With reference to the MAIA mission often seen in news, which of the following statement is correct?
options: a) It aims to utilise a satellite instrument to investigate harmful impacts of UV radiation on marine organisms.
b) It is a satellite mission to understand the effects of different types of particle pollution on human health.
c) It is a mission mode project of the Union Environment Ministry to encourage afforestation in urban areas.
d) It is a mission to study radiation in the Arctic to better understand its impact on melting glaciers.
mnemonic_hint: MAIA: 'My Air, Impact Assessment'—a mission to see how air particles impact our health.

questionText: Which of the following market-based approaches are provided under the Paris Agreement adopted in 2015? 1. Internationally Transferred Mitigation Outcomes (ITMOs) 2. Joint Implementation (JI) 3. Sustainable Development Mechanism (SDM) 4. International Emissions Trading (IET) mechanism Select the correct answer using the code given below:
sub_topic: International Climate Agreements and Carbon Markets
concepts: Transition from Kyoto Protocol to Paris Agreement
mnemonic_hint: Remember '6.2 ITMOs' (International transfers) and '6.4 SDM' (Sustainable Development) as the two pillars of Paris Article 6.

questionText: Consider the following statements with reference to the ‘Arth Ganga’ initiative: 1. It was launched under the Namami Ganga Program. 2. It aims for a stable economic development model to strengthen the river-people connection through an economic bridge. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mnemonic_hint: Think of 'Arth' as 'Artha' (Wealth/Economy) flowing through the Ganga to connect people to the river.

questionText: Why is plant called Prosopis Chilensis often mentioned in news?
options: a) It is used as a natural substitute of synthetic Antioxidants
b) It is used to create biodegradable plastic
c) It tends to reduce biodiversity in the area in which it grows
mnemonic_hint: Think of 'Prosopis' as a 'Pro-pests' plant that aggressively takes over the area, reducing biodiversity.

questionText: Which of the following were outcomes of the United Nations Conference on the Environment of 1972? 1. Adoption of Stockholm Declaration 2. Action Plan for the Human Environment 3. Creation of United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) 4. Proposed 5th June as World Environment Day Select the correct answer using the code given below:
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'S-A-U-W': Stockholm Declaration, Action Plan, UNEP, World Environment Day.

questionText: Which one of the following best describes the term ‘Shallow Ecologism’?
options: a) An approach that requires a drastic change in the way humans interact with nature
b) A philosophy that believes in specific changes in daily lifestyle of humans to minimize the damage to the environment
c) A set of sustainable practices to increase fish production in shallow ocean ecosystems
d) A geoengineering technique to reduce the intensity of incoming solar radiation
mnemonic_hint: Think 'Shallow' as 'Self-centered'—it only fixes the surface to keep humans comfortable, unlike 'Deep' ecology which values nature for its own sake.

questionText: With reference to the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP), consider the following statements: 1. It is a NITI Aayog initiative with the collaboration of Central Pollution Control Board. 2. It targets a 20 % to 30 % reduction in Particulate Matter across the country by 2024. 3. It has been launched focusing on overall pollution reduction in all the districts in India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
keywords: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'NCAP-MoEFCC' (not NITI) and that it targets 'Non-attainment' cities, not every district.

questionText: With reference to the National Board for Wildlife (NBWL), consider the following statements: 1. The Standing Committee of the NBWL chaired by the Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. 2. Its approval is mandatory for any alteration or denotification of Tiger Reserves under the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'PM-NBWL': The Prime Minister chairs the Board, but the Minister chairs the Standing Committee.

questionText: The term ‘loss and damage’ is used in the climate change negotiations process to refer to the harms caused by anthropogenic climate change. In this context, consider the following statements regarding ‘loss and damage’: 1. The term ‘Loss and Damage’ was first used during the outcome of the Earth Summit in 1992. 2. Warsaw International Mechanism on Loss and Damage (WIM) has developed funding mechanisms to help developing countries manage loss and damage. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'WIM' as 'Warsaw International Mechanism'—it's the 'WIM' that helps developing countries win against climate loss.

questionText: With reference to ‘Energy Transition Accelerator (ETA)’, consider the following statements: 1. It is a carbon offset program launched by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change. 2. It aims to fund renewable energy projects in developing countries to help them shift to renewable power sources. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'ETA' as 'Energy Transition Accelerator'—it's a US-led initiative, not IPCC, to speed up the shift to green power.

questionText: Consider the following pairs: Climate change convention Major outcomes 1. Sharm el-Sheikh Summit Food and Agriculture for Sustainable Transformation initiative 2. Madrid Summit Climate Ambition Alliance 3. Glasgow Summit Green Climate Fund. How many pair/s is/are correctly matched?
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'FAST-Sharm' (Food/Ag at Egypt), 'Alliance-Madrid' (Ambition), and note that GCF was established much earlier (2010) than Glasgow (2021).

questionText: Consider the following Statement regarding National Mission for Clean Ganga: 1. It was registered as a society on 12th August 2011 under the Societies Registration Act 1860. 2. It acted as the implementation arm of National Ganga Council. 3. It was constituted under the provisions of the Water Pollution Act, 1974. How many of the above statements are correct?
mnemonic_hint: NMCG is a 'Society' under the 'Environment' Act (EPA 1986), not the 'Water' Act.

questionText: Consider the following: 1. African Market Carbon Initiative 2. Glasgow Breakthrough Agenda 3. Global Goal on Adaptation (GGA) 4. Buildings Breakthrough Initiative 5. Coalition for High Ambition Multilevel Partnerships (CHAMP) How many of the above are the key outcomes of 28th Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change?
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'C-G-B-C-B' for COP28: CHAMP, GGA, Breakthroughs (Glasgow & Buildings), and Carbon (African Market).

questionText: With reference to Right to repair, consider the following: 1. It provides consumers a legal framework to demand free repair from manufacturers of electronic devices. 2. Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology has introduced Right to Repair India portal recently. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'R2R' as Repair-to-Reuse: It is about access to manuals and parts, not a mandate for free repairs.

questionText: With reference to engagements of India in COP 28, consider the following statements: 1. India and UAE launched ‘Green Credits Programme’ at COP-28 in alignment with Mission LiFE. 2. India launched the Global River Cities Alliance (GRCA) covering 275+ global river cities for sustainable river-centric development. 3. India advocated for phasing out of coal-generated electricity in the near term. How many of the above statements are correct?
sub_topic: International Climate Negotiations and India's Initiatives
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'GRCA' as 'Global River Cities Alliance'—India leads the flow for sustainable cities at COP28.

questionText: Consider the following Statements regarding Biodiversity Heritage Sites (BHS): 1. They are declared under Environment Protection Act, 1986 2. State Governments notifies areas of biodiversity importance as BHS. 3. Nallur Tamarind Grove is situated in Kerala. How many of the above statements are correct?
concepts: Legal framework for biodiversity conservation in India
Institutional roles of State Governments in environmental protection
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'Bio-State-2002': Biodiversity Heritage Sites are notified by State Governments under the Biological Diversity Act of 2002, not the 1986 EPA.

questionText: With reference to Carbon bombs often seen in news, which of the following statement is correct?
options: a) Non-inclusion of environmental costs in the Annual Financial Statements of a country
b) Earth-saving fireworks that shoot out emissions free play works during celebrations.
c) Explosive solutions that convert greenhouse gases into harmless bubbles for the ozone layer.
d) An oil or gas project resulting in at least a billion tonnes of CO2 emissions over its lifetime
mnemonic_hint: Think of a 'Carbon Bomb' as a 'Billion-ton Blast' of CO2 from a single fossil fuel project.

questionText: Consider the following Statement Regarding C-40 Initiative: 1. It is a global network of nearly 100 mayors of the world’s leading cities, united in action to confront the climate crisis. 2. It is under the aegis of the United Nation Environment Programme. 3. They follow the Co-chair method, which requires one mayor each from the Global North and South. How many of the above statements are correct?
mnemonic_hint: C40 is a 'City-led' network, not a UN-led one; remember 'C40 is a City Club, not a UN Hub'.

questionText: Consider the following statement with reference to SECURE Himalayas Project: 1. The aim of this project is to conserve the habitats of snow leopards. 2. It is jointly implemented by the Union Environment ministry and United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP). 3. Project is funded by the Global Environment Facility. 4. Snow leopard’s habitat range extends across the mountainous regions of 12 countries across Asia. How many of the above statements are correct?
keywords: Ministry of Environment Forest and Climate Change
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'SECURE' as Snow leopard, Environment, Conservation, United Nations, Range, and Ecosystems.

questionText: Consider the following Pairs regarding segregation of Waste as per Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules: Colour Waste Covered 1. Red Anatomical, Chemical Waste 2. Blue Glass waste and metallic implants 3. Yellow Contaminated plastic waste 4. Black Hazardous and other waste How many pair/s is/are correctly matched?
mnemonic_hint: Remember 'Y-A-C' (Yellow: Anatomical/Chemical) and 'R-P' (Red: Plastic/Contaminated) to avoid the common trap of swapping them.
